title: Same-family additive-eight with complete live checked predicates

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Define v_N=min(d_plan,c+1+sum[(T_u-1)*(I_u-1)]); fallback v_N=u_N=N+1. For EVERY integer N>=0, C_B2(Trim_N)>=4N-8v_N+8>=4N-8u_N+8. Nonfallback v_N>=3 permits the fully supplied additive8 gate theorem; its complete RamseyR/S, formula, exception and predecessor predicates are validated by the declared audit. At EVERY sufficiently large integer N, v_N<=u_N<=2^ceil(D_trim Z), D_trim=139829/50000=2.79658,Z=ceil(L^(3/4))*ceil(B^(1/4)),L=ceil(log2 N),B=ceil(log2(L+1)). Thus for each fixed epsilon>0, C_B2(Trim_N)>=4N-N^epsilon at ALL sufficiently large integer lengths and this SAME eligible family has liminf C_B2(Trim_N)/N>=4.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}
